subject: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler - follow-up & next tests
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler (next steps)

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

1) What we heard from you:
- Priority: predictable throughput for customer-facing APIs (latency SLOs at p95 < 150ms for 2k rps burst).
- Concern: hyperscaler spot/preemptible instances cause noisy neighbors and unpredictable throttling.
- Compliance: need audit logs + customer data isolation for production.

2) How Redwood maps to that:
- Dedicated GPU pools (reserved capacity) with SLA-backed throughput and network isolation.
- Smart routing + automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants to keep traffic live during capacity events.
- Audit logs, KMS integrations, and private deployment options for regulated data.

3) Suggested next tests (to validate differences vs hyperscaler):
- Load test (baseline): 2k rps sustained 30m, measure p50/p95/p99 latency and failure rates.
- Preemption scenario: simulate instance loss and measure failover time and error-rate impact.
- Cost delta: run same workload on hyperscaler reserved + burst config vs Redwood Dedicated with batching/caching profiles and report $/1000 tokens.

Next steps:
- I’ll send a short comparison doc and a quote for a 3-month reserved pool we discussed. (See attachments)
- If that looks good, run a joint load test next week — Marissa, can you confirm availability for Wed/Thu?

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler (next steps)

Thanks Markus — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions before we lock in tests:

- For the reserved pool, can you confirm the SLA guarantees around throughput and availability? Do you have historical metrics for sustained 24h periods?
- How do you handle preemption/failover? With hyperscalers we’ve seen minutes of degradation when instances come back.
- On cost: can you show an apples-to-apples estimate including egress, instance amortization, and typical batching gains?

Also, procurement asked for a reference architecture and a short statement on how data is isolated for multi-tenant setups. We’ll likely need that to start legal review.

If possible can we schedule the load test Thu 2026-03-25 10:00–11:30 PT?

—Sarah
Head of Platform, Acme AI
sarah.lee@acme-ai.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, procurement@acme-ai.com
Date: 2026-03-22T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler (next steps)

Sarah — great questions. Quick answers and what I’m attaching: a short comparison doc and a draft MAL/quote for the reserved pool.

SLA and guarantees:
- We offer a Dedicated SLA tied to reserved capacity commitments: uptime SLA 99.9% and throughput SLOs per-pool (we’ll size the pool for your 2k rps target). SLA includes credits for measurable drops below throughput targets.
- Historical metrics: we can provide anonymized cluster-level dashboards for sustained 24h windows; I’ve included a sample dashboard screenshot in the comparison doc.

Preemption / failover:
- On hyperscalers: preemptions are handled at the infra level and can cause cold restarts; customers report multi-minute disruption depending on warmup.
- Redwood Dedicated: no preemption for reserved pools. For Hosted tiers we run multi-variant fallbacks; for Dedicated we recommend pinned pools + cross-region standby to meet your p95 SLOs.

Cost comparison notes:
- Attached is an apples-to-apples sample using your workload assumptions: we model instance costs, orchestration, egress, and realistic batching gains. Key point: Dedicated eliminates waste from preemption and often reduces $/1000 tokens once batching & KV caching are applied.

Data isolation:
- Dedicated pools are logically isolated; for Private deployments we support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. The attached doc includes a one-page architecture diagram for procurement.

Proposed next steps and logistics:
- Load test: Thu 2026-03-25 10:00–11:30 PT works for us — Dylan will run the test harness; please share a small sample prompt set and auth token for the sandbox.
- Pre-test: we’ll provision a 3-node reserved pool for the window, run baseline, then simulate an instance loss to measure failover.
- Post-test: we’ll deliver a findings report and cost comparison.

I’ve attached: Redwood_Dedicated_vs_Hyperscaler_Comparison.pdf and ACME-MAL-quote-20260324.pdf (draft).

See you Thu — Markus
